Flatten grafted phylogenies into a single set of phylogenies

Source: R/flatten_grafted_phylogenies.R
flatten_grafted_phylogenies.Rd

The grafting functions return a list with one element per stochastic map when they are used with several maps (a "multiSimmap"), each element being a phylogeny or a set of phylogenies (one per simulation). This function flattens such an output into a single object of class "multiPhylo", which can be used directly by the functions that expect a set of phylogenies under this class (e.g., from the packages ape or phytools). The associated stochastic map ID, the simulation ID and the seed of each phylogeny are kept, so the phylogenies can still be traced back and selected.

The arguments maps and simulations can be used to subset the object and retain only a specific sets of grafted phylogenies based on their associated stochastic map, and/or their simulation index.

Additionally, the function can trim out the updated stochastic maps stored in the $simmap element of each grafted function to save memory space if those updated grafted stochastic maps are not required for downstream analyses.

Usage

flatten_grafted_phylogenies(
  phy_grafted,
  maps = NULL,
  simulations = NULL,
  keep_simmap = TRUE
)

Arguments

phy_grafted

The output of phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() or phylograftR::graft_missing_clades(): a list with one element per stochastic map (each a "phylo" or a "multiPhylo"), a "multiPhylo", or a "phylo". A "multiPhylo" or a "phylo" object is already flat, but the function can still be used to select a subset of phylogenies and remove their associated simmaps if requested.

maps

Character vector. Names of the maps to keep (the names of the elements of the list, as in the column map of the attribute "phylogenies"). Default is NULL, which keeps all the maps. The function stops if some names are not found.

simulations

Integer vector. Indices of the simulations to keep (the numbers in the names "sim_k" of the phylogenies, which are the same in each map: 1 for the first simulation of each map, etc.). Default is NULL, which keeps all the simulations.

keep_simmap

Logical. Whether to keep the element $simmap (the updated simmap) of the phylogenies, if they have one. Set to FALSE to save memory when the stochastic maps are not needed in downstream analyses. Default is TRUE.

Value

If phy_grafted is an object of class "phylo", the output is also a phylogeny, with its $simmap removed if keep_simmap = FALSE (otherwise unchanged). Otherwise, the output is an object of class "multiPhylo" with all the phylogenies selected, and the following attributes:

  • "phylogenies": data.frame with one row per phylogeny, in the order of the object, with the columns name, map (NA if no map was used), simulation (index of the simulation) and seed (NA if unknown).

  • "seeds": named integer vector with the seed of each phylogeny (NULL if the seeds are unknown, i.e., if the grafting was run with seed = NULL).

  • "failed": data.frame with the simulations that failed in the maps kept, with the columns map, seed and reason (0 row if none). Not filtered by simulations.

  • "failed_maps": data.frame with the maps dropped from the output of the grafting function because none of their simulations could be obtained, with the columns map and reason (0 row if none).

Details

The phylogenies are returned in the order of the input (map by map, then simulation by simulation), with their names as in the input: the names of the maps for a list of phylogenies (one simulation per map), and "<map>_sim_k" for a list of sets of phylogenies (several simulations per map). If two phylogenies have the same name, the names are made unique with a warning.

Each phylogeny keeps its attributes "map" and "seed". When maps and simulations are used, the selection is applied to all the phylogenies together: the phylogenies kept are the ones from the maps in maps and with the simulation index in simulations.

See also

Other functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() to graft taxa based on target clades and excluded subclades using the list.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_clades() to graft groups of missing taxa as sister clades using the list.

Author

Maël Doré

Examples

# --- Prepare data --- #

# Load backbone phylogeny, associated simmap, and missing taxa list
data(toy_backbone)
data(toy_simmap)
data(toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_states)

# Create a toy backbone phylogeny, with a set of 3 stochastic maps of a trait
tip_states <- phytools::getStates(toy_simmap, type = "tips")
had_seed <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)
if (had_seed) old_seed <- get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)
set.seed(118)
toy_multiSimmap <- phytools::make.simmap(toy_backbone, tip_states,
                                         model = "ER", nsim = 3, message = FALSE)
if (had_seed)
{ assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = globalenv())
} else { rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()) }

# --- Graft missing taxa --- #

# Graft with the 3 maps and 2 simulations per map as constraints:
# the output is a list with one element per map hosting 2 simulations each.
grafted_list <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = toy_backbone,
                              missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_states,
                              simmap = toy_multiSimmap, allowed_states = c("blue", "green"),
                              method = "BD_clades", nb_simulations = 2,
                              verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)
names(grafted_list)
#> [1] "map_1" "map_2" "map_3"
str(grafted_list, 2)
#> List of 3
#>  $ map_1:Class "multiPhylo"
#> List of 2
#>   ..$ map_1_sim_1:List of 7
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "class")= chr "phylo"
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "order")= chr "cladewise"
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "seed")= int 1234
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "map")= chr "map_1"
#>   ..$ map_1_sim_2:List of 7
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "class")= chr "phylo"
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "order")= chr "cladewise"
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "seed")= int 488349520
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "map")= chr "map_1"
#>   ..- attr(*, "seeds")= Named num [1:2] 1.23e+03 4.88e+08
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:2] "map_1_sim_1" "map_1_sim_2"
#>   ..- attr(*, "failed")='data.frame':	0 obs. of  2 variables:
#>  $ map_2:Class "multiPhylo"
#> List of 2
#>   ..$ map_2_sim_1:List of 7
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "class")= chr "phylo"
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "order")= chr "cladewise"
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "seed")= int 1234
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "map")= chr "map_2"
#>   ..$ map_2_sim_2:List of 7
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "class")= chr "phylo"
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "order")= chr "cladewise"
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "seed")= int 488349520
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "map")= chr "map_2"
#>   ..- attr(*, "seeds")= Named num [1:2] 1.23e+03 4.88e+08
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:2] "map_2_sim_1" "map_2_sim_2"
#>   ..- attr(*, "failed")='data.frame':	0 obs. of  2 variables:
#>  $ map_3:Class "multiPhylo"
#> List of 2
#>   ..$ map_3_sim_1:List of 7
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "class")= chr "phylo"
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "order")= chr "cladewise"
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "seed")= int 1234
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "map")= chr "map_3"
#>   ..$ map_3_sim_2:List of 7
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "class")= chr "phylo"
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "order")= chr "cladewise"
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "seed")= int 488349520
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "map")= chr "map_3"
#>   ..- attr(*, "seeds")= Named num [1:2] 1.23e+03 4.88e+08
#>   .. ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:2] "map_3_sim_1" "map_3_sim_2"
#>   ..- attr(*, "failed")='data.frame':	0 obs. of  2 variables:
#>  - attr(*, "failed_maps")='data.frame':	0 obs. of  2 variables:
#>   ..$ map   : chr(0) 
#>   ..$ reason: chr(0) 

# --- Flatten the output --- #

# Flatten the output into a single multiPhylo with the 6 grafted phylogenies
grafted_phys <- flatten_grafted_phylogenies(grafted_list)
names(grafted_phys)
#> [1] "map_1_sim_1" "map_1_sim_2" "map_2_sim_1" "map_2_sim_2" "map_3_sim_1"
#> [6] "map_3_sim_2"
# The map, simulation and seed of each phylogeny are stored as an attribute
attr(grafted_phys, "phylogenies")
#>          name   map simulation      seed
#> 1 map_1_sim_1 map_1          1      1234
#> 2 map_1_sim_2 map_1          2 488349520
#> 3 map_2_sim_1 map_2          1      1234
#> 4 map_2_sim_2 map_2          2 488349520
#> 5 map_3_sim_1 map_3          1      1234
#> 6 map_3_sim_2 map_3          2 488349520

# --- Flatten the output, subset, and remove simmaps all-at-once --- #

# Keep the first simulation of two maps only, without the simmaps (to save memory)
grafted_subset <- flatten_grafted_phylogenies(grafted_list, maps = c("map_1", "map_3"),
                                              simulations = 1, keep_simmap = FALSE)
attr(grafted_subset, "phylogenies")
#>          name   map simulation seed
#> 1 map_1_sim_1 map_1          1 1234
#> 2 map_3_sim_1 map_3          1 1234

# Use the set of phylogenies with functions that expect a multiPhylo,
# e.g., to compute the tree heights.
sapply(grafted_phys, function (x) max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(x)))
#> map_1_sim_1 map_1_sim_2 map_2_sim_1 map_2_sim_2 map_3_sim_1 map_3_sim_2 
#>          50          50          50          50          50          50
